description: Every maximal run of consecutive far-commutations sharing a high letter, in the Bokut-Shiao corner's a <= b chain, is a RIGHT transport: the high letter sits at the rewrite position throughout, the position advances by exactly one per step, every letter passed is at least two below it, and the run's net effect is a ++ (x :: (w ++ b)) -> a ++ (w ++ (x :: b)). That is farComm_transport_right, NOT farComm_transport_left.

parameters.unified_blueprint: top-level block and small(a) obey ONE blueprint: W = descWord (min(h-2, j1+1)) j_eff, B = descWord (h-1) (j1+1) ++ T. Top-level: j_eff = j2, T = [s_i]. small(a): j_eff = j1, T = descWord j1 j2. The tail T must therefore be a PARAMETER of any lemma meant to cover both -- hardcoding [s_i] covers only the former.
parameters.level_blueprint: level with high letter s_h:  W = descWord (min(h-2, j1+1)) j2,  B = descWord (h-1) (j1+1) ++ [s_i].  Uniform over every level of every block, on and off the diagonal.
parameters.block_as_three_lean_steps: h = j1+1 (W = descWord (j1-1) j2); h = j1+2 (W = descWord j1 j2); then blockTransportRight with X = descWord i (j1+3), W = descWord (j1+1) j2, B = descWord (j1+2) (j1+1) ++ [s_i]
parameters.block_levels_off_diagonal: b > a: a levels, level k (high = j1+k) passes min(b-a-1+k, b-a+2) letters -- exactly 2 short levels, all the rest at the cap
parameters.block_levels_on_diagonal: b = a: a-1 levels, level k passes min(k, 2) letters -- 1 short level, the rest at the cap

caveats: Measured over a = 2..6 and b in {a, a+1, a+3} only, and against the reduction the engine's deg-lex strategy happens to produce. A Lean proof may follow a different chain.

Runs are grouped by high letter AND by same-term continuation. Grouping on the high letter alone is wrong: an element becomes multi-term the moment the quadratic rule fires, so two adjacent chain steps can rewrite different terms. Without the same-term test this script reported a spurious failing run at a = b = 2 -- steps 10 and 11 both apply F(0,2), but to words of length 6 and 5.

This says each run IS a right-transport. It does not say the Lean lemma applies as-is: farComm_transport_right carries the UNRESTRICTED collision hypothesis (every split of w, including the one naming the transport's own final word). farComm_transport_left needed a _sources variant with u != [] for exactly that reason in the a > b regime, so the right-hand mirror may need one too. Not measurable here -- it is a property of the bystanding terms, not of the run.
